question: Why did the EdgeForce team change the rollback procedure for model updates, and what had gone wrong with rollbacks before that?
answer:
**What went wrong before:** EdgeForce had a "Model Update Rollback Error" bug — when a model update failed, the transaction management system did not correctly revert the changes. This left devices with incomplete or corrupted models, causing inaccurate insights for customers (impacting CUST-0076).

**Why the procedure was changed:** The root cause was identified as a flaw in the transaction management logic that failed to properly track and revert changes during a failed update. To fix this, the team revised the transaction management logic to ensure all changes are accurately tracked and rolled back if an update fails, so the device returns to its previous stable state. Extra checks/safeguards were added to maintain data integrity, and the fix was verified by simulating update failures and confirming all changes were correctly reverted (see PR: https://github.com/salesforce/EdgeForce/pull/50). The team also looked at Kubernetes' similar "Failed Rollback of Deployment Updates" issue/PR for additional insight into handling rollbacks.

**Why the procedure was changed:** The root cause was identified as a flaw in the transaction management logic that failed to properly track and revert changes during a failed update. To fix this, the team revised the transaction management logic to ensure all changes are accurately tracked and rolled back if an update fails, so the device returns to its previous stable state. Extra checks/safeguards were added to maintain data integrity, and the fix was verified by simulating update failures and confirming all changes were correctly reverted (see PR: https://github.com/salesforce/EdgeForce/pull/50). The team also looked at Kubernetes' similar "Failed Rollback of Deployment Updates" issue/PR for additional insight into handling rollbacks.
